statement: Every full-dimensional finite-volume convex hyperbolic 4-polytope whose face lattice is that of the 4-cube, whose vertices are finite or ideal (with no hyperideal or truncated substitute), and whose dihedral angles all equal alpha_0 = arccos(1/3), is isometric to the regular ideal equiangular 4-cube C^4_(alpha_0), represented in the Klein ball by the closure [-1/2,1/2]^4.
contribution: A complete Lorentz-Gram proof of the frozen endpoint case omitted by the cited source: ideal-vertex null sums force the four opposite-pair difference normals to span a positive 4-space, the sum normals then force all opposite Gram entries to be -5/3, and a relation-safe time-orientation-preserving Lorentz isometry carries all eight oriented halfspaces to the explicit Klein cube. This is a proposer claim awaiting fresh referee review; the bounded source search does not assert novelty or priority.
